purpose: Roadmap phase 5: repeatable startup baseline and a rejected Zod jitless A/B
method: scripts/profile-startup.mjs --samples=10 --fresh-browser against vite preview (port 4173); cache disabled; 390x844 mobile emulation; 4 Mbps / 100 ms RTT; 4x CPU. Readiness = enabled Begin + decoded art. After an initial pair, baseline and jitless builds were interleaved (baseline, jitless, baseline, jitless).

runs.label: baseline
runs.method: 10 sequential fresh browser contexts, each in a newly launched browser; cache disabled; 390x844; 4 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up / 100 ms RTT; 4x CPU throughout. Readiness requires enabled Begin and decoded art. ResourceTiming and Long Tasks observation enabled; no CPU profiler. Every sample retained; summary uses nearest-rank percentiles.

runs.label: baseline-shared
runs.method: 10 sequential fresh browser contexts in one browser; cache disabled; 390x844; 4 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up / 100 ms RTT; 4x CPU throughout. Readiness requires enabled Begin and decoded art. conclusion: Baseline medians 2158/2081/2135 ms (shared-browser 2108 ms); jitless medians 2085/2169/2175 ms. No measurable improvement, so z.config({ jitless: true }) was not shipped. All samples are far below the historical 4.6-27 s captures; host contention at capture time, not the build, likely dominated earlier variance. Chromium emulation on a shared Linux host, not reference-device acceptance.

notAttempted.workerPrefetch: The worker chunk arrives in 30-65 ms and the profiler disables the HTTP cache, so a prefetch could not be measured and would save at most ~2-3%.
notAttempted.lazyPostBeginScreens: Offline Begin requires those chunks before case-ready; with a ~2.1 s median the expected gain does not justify restructuring App.tsx now.
